newsitem.title: USA: Malcolm X widow undergoes skin operation.
newsitem.headline: Malcolm X widow undergoes skin operation.

text.p: The widow of slain civil rights leader Malcolm X, badly burned in a fire allegedly set by her troubled grandson, is undergoing skin graft surgery, hospital officials said on Wednesday.
Betty Shabazz, 63, is in extremely critical but stable condition in a New York hospital. She suffered third-degree burns over 80 percent of her body in the fire early on Sunday.

A team of six doctors planned to remove about 20 percent of her dead skin. The operation at Jacobi Hospital in the Bronx borough of New York City will last about two hours and will be overseen by Dr. Bruce Greenstein, director of the burn unit, a hospital spokeswoman said.

"Because of the large area of the burn and the limited skin available for grafting the burn wound will be covered with Integra, an artifical skin product," Greenstein told reporters. He also planned to take a sample of Shabazz's skin to be cultured and grown in a laboratory for grafting later.
A third-degree burn is one that extends deep into the skin's underlying tissue.

Shabazz's 12-year-old grandson, Malcolm Shabazz, named after his controversial grandfather, is accused of setting the fire at her Yonkers, New York, apartment. A judge on Tuesday ordered him to undergo medical and psychological evaluations before returning to Westchester Family Court on Friday.
Law enforcement officials allege Malcolm splashed fuel at the front door of Shabazz's apartment and set it afire. He had been staying there for the last three weeks.

Bill Tatum, publisher of the Amsterdam News and a family friend, described Malcolm as "a disturbed child of trauma." He said the boy was angry with his grandmother and wanted her to send him back to his mother, Qubilah Shabazz, 36.

Qubilah Shabazz, a daughter of Malcolm X and Betty Shabazz, saw her father assassinated at Harlem's Audubon Ballroom in 1965. She was charged in 1995 with plotting to kill Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, whom her mother had accused of playing a role in Malcolm X's assassination. Federal prosecutors dismissed the case last month.

The Daily News on Wednesday said the boy had told police he thought his grandmother's death would hasten his return to Texas, where his mother lives in San Antonio. "He said he wanted to kill her," it quoted a police source as saying.
